keyVerseText: According to the custom of the priest's office, his lot was to burn incense when he went into the temple of the Lord.
rootMeaning: The word ἱερατεία (hierateía) derives from the verb ἱερατεύω (hierateúō), which means to execute the priest's office or to perform the functions of a priest. This root emphasizes the active role and duties involved in priestly service rather than merely the title or status. Thus, the literal sense of ἱερατεία conveys not just the concept of priesthood but the actual exercise and responsibility of priestly functions, highlighting the sacred service aspect inherent in the term.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, ἱερατεία appears only twice, consistently referring to the office or function of the priesthood. It is translated either as "of the priest's office" or "the office of the priesthood," indicating a focus on the official role and duties assigned to priests. This limited but consistent usage underscores the term's precise meaning, anchoring it firmly in the context of sacerdotal service and the responsibilities associated with it.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἱερατεία as the active priestly office enriches our grasp of how Scripture views the role of priests, not merely as a title but as a sacred calling to serve God and His people. This term reflects the divine appointment and functional service that priests perform, which ultimately points to Christ's perfect and eternal priesthood. Recognizing the priesthood as a living office helps believers appreciate the gravity and holiness involved in mediating between God and humanity, a role fulfilled once and for all in Jesus. Thus, ἱερατεία invites reflection on the nature of spiritual service and the continuity of God's redemptive plan through priestly ministry.
keyVerseReflection: Luke 1:9 states, "According to the custom of the priest's office, his lot was to burn incense when he went into the temple of the Lord." Here, ἱερατεία highlights the formal and divinely established duties of the priest. The phrase underscores that the priest's actions are not arbitrary but rooted in a sacred office with prescribed functions. This enriches the verse by showing that priestly service involves specific, God-ordained responsibilities that serve as a foreshadowing of Christ's ultimate priestly work.
